title: Metadata - Behavior
text_content: File-based metadata has the higher priority and will override any config-based metadata.

title: Metadata - Default Fields
text_content:
There are two default `` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
The [https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
The [https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
Good to know: You can overwrite the default [/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.

title: Metadata - Merging
text_content:
Following the [#ordering](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are shallowly merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are replaced based on their ordering.
This means metadata with nested fields such as [/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are overwritten by the last segment to define them.

Metadata - JSON-LD
text_content:
[https://json-ld.org/](https://json-ld.org/) is a format for structured data that can be used by search engines to understand your content. For example, you can use it to describe a person, an event, an organization, a movie, a book, a recipe, and many other types of entities.
Our current recommendation for JSON-LD is to render structured data as a `` tag in your `` or `` components. For example:
You can validate and test your structured data with the [https://search.google.com/test/rich-results](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) for Google or the generic [https://validator.schema.org/](https://validator.schema.org/).
You can type your JSON-LD with TypeScript using community packages like [https://www.npmjs.com/package/schema-dts](https://www.npmjs.com/package/schema-dts):
